Based on my code search, the text "Unavailable" doesn't come from the iOS app's own strings — it's not in the localization files for replies. Here's what I found about the reply loading pipeline and where the issue likely originates:

The reply detail state machine (TimelineItemReplyDetails.swift):

.notLoaded → app calls fetchDetails on the SDK
.loading → waiting for SDK response
.loaded → shows the reply bubble content
.error → SDK returned an error (message stored, but not shown in UI — just a loading placeholder)
The SDK-to-app mapping (RoomTimelineItemFactory.swift:847):


case .unavailable:
    return .init(details: .notLoaded(eventID: details.eventId()), isThreaded: isThreaded)
When the Rust SDK returns .unavailable for the replied-to event, it becomes .notLoaded, which triggers a fetch. If that fetch also fails/returns unavailable, it cycles into .error.

The "Unavailable" text you're seeing is almost certainly coming from the Rust SDK layer itself, not from Swift UI code. Most likely causes:

Encrypted history — If the room is encrypted and your device isn't verified, the replied-to event can't be decrypted. Check for the encrypted history banner (screen_room_encrypted_history_banner).

SDK can't fetch the event — The replied-to event is on a federated server that's down or temporarily unreachable. The SDK returns an error string containing "Unavailable" which ends up in the .error(eventID:, message:) case.

Event outside history visibility — The replied-to event predates your room membership and the history visibility setting prevents loading it.

Send failure — If the send itself fails, check logs for errors in TimelineProxy.sendMessage around timeline.sendReply(msg:eventId:) (TimelineProxy.swift:406).

To diagnose: enable verbose logging (MXLog.verbose) and look for errors in getLoadedReplyDetails or fetchDetails calls to see what the SDK is returning.
